title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 77–78
description: Advanced language for memories, nostalgia, regret and remorse; expressing agreement, dissent, social division and negotiated compromise.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study from the user-provided edition. Teaching targets, exercises and the answer key informed the selection; translations, examples and explanatory notes are original and do not reproduce textbook dialogues or exercise passages.

audit.scope: Unit 77 sections A–B, Common mistakes and exercises 77.1–77.4; Unit 78 sections A–C, Language help and exercises 78.1–78.3; corresponding answer-key entries.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British IPA only on selected targets where reliable; blank IPA avoids unverified transcriptions of extended expressions.
audit.languagePolicy: English for all learner-facing fields except the Brazilian Portuguese translations in pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Reviewed the teaching pages, exercise pages and relevant answer-key entries; independently wrote and checked examples and meaning notes; compared JSON keys and types with the canonical reference and ran static item and speech-target validation.
audit.limitations: No bundled MP3 audio. Import in VocabLab, browser-based TTS and pronunciation recognition have not been tested. Some brief speechText values are illustrative spoken forms of open-ended patterns.

units.title: Unit 77 — Reminiscences and regrets
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 77. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Memory and reflection · reminiscence, regret and nostalgia
learningObjectives: Recall past events with appropriate expressions for vivid, vague and returning memories.
Distinguish remembering, being reminded of something and losing touch with people.
Recognise nostalgic language and its tendency to idealise the past.
Use regret, remorse, rue, lament and mourn with appropriate meaning, register and grammatical patterns.

sectionsChecked: A · Looking back: sharing memories and numbered explanatory notes
B · Expressing regret and literary alternatives

items.pt: desatualizado sobre; sem acompanhar o que acontece com
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: Since moving overseas, she has been out of touch with developments at her old university.
items.note: Being out of touch with a topic means not having recent information about it; also used of lost social contact.
items.speechText: out of touch with recent events

items.pt: perder contato com alguém
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: I lost touch with several former colleagues when our department closed.
items.note: Lose touch with someone describes a change; be out of touch describes the continuing state.

items.pt: o que aconteceu com; que fim levou
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: I sometimes wonder what became of the journalist who interviewed us years ago.
items.note: Ask what became of someone to find out what happened to them later; somewhat reflective or literary.

items.pt: se bem me lembro; se minha memória não falha
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: If I recall, the original proposal had a much smaller budget.
items.note: A cautious way to introduce a recollection that may not be completely reliable.

items.pt: recordar; lembrar-se de
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: I cannot recall exactly where we first discussed the proposal.
items.note: Recall is relatively formal compared with remember; it can take a noun or a clause.

items.pt: voltar mentalmente ao passado; recordar
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: When I think back to my first year abroad, I remember feeling both excited and anxious.
items.note: Think back to a time or event means deliberately remember it.

items.pt: olhar para trás; refletir sobre o passado
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: Looking back, I realise that changing careers was the right decision.
items.note: Often used when reassessing past choices with the benefit of hindsight.

items.pt: pensando agora no passado; relembrando
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: Thinking back, the early warning signs were clear to everyone except us.
items.note: Sentence-initial phrase introducing a reconsideration of past events.

items.pt: ter alguma notícia de alguém
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: Have you heard anything of Marta since she finished her research fellowship?
items.note: The source uses hear anything of someone in questions about news of their life or whereabouts.

items.pt: receber alguma notícia; saber de algo
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: After his departure, we did not hear a thing about how the negotiations ended.
items.note: Often appears in negative sentences, emphasising a complete absence of news.

items.pt: acabar fazendo algo; terminar por fazer algo
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: After training as a biologist, she ended up working in science journalism.
items.note: End up + -ing describes the eventual outcome of a process, sometimes an unexpected one.

items.pt: fazer alguém lembrar-se de algo
items.example: The smell of fresh paint reminded me of the house where I grew up.
items.note: Use remind someone of something: the thing causes the memory in another person.

items.pt: lembrar-se de; recordar
items.example: I still remember our first conversation after the conference.
items.note: Remember describes having or retrieving a memory; do not use remember me of to mean remind me of.

items.pt: transportar alguém mentalmente a uma lembrança
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: That familiar melody took me back to summer evenings at my grandparents’ house.
items.note: Figurative phrase for vividly recalling a particular earlier time.
items.speechText: take me back to my childhood

items.pt: uma lembrança vaga; recordação pouco nítida
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: I have a vague memory of meeting the author at a book launch years ago.
items.note: Vague describes a memory lacking precise details; commonly followed by of.

items.word: it all came back to me
items.pt: tudo voltou à minha memória; lembrei-me de tudo
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: When she mentioned the village, it all came back to me.
items.note: A sudden return of previously forgotten details or events.

items.pt: voltar à memória de alguém
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: The missing details gradually came back to him as he reviewed the photographs.
items.note: A memory or detail can come back to someone, often without deliberate effort.

items.pt: destacar-se na memória; ser o que mais lembro
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: What stands out in my mind is the extraordinary kindness of the local volunteers.
items.note: The most memorable feature of an experience; stick out in my mind is a variant.

items.pt: ficar marcado na minha memória; sobressair nas lembranças
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: The closing remarks still stick out in my mind after all these years.
items.note: Informal alternative to stand out in my mind; both focus on a vivid memory.

items.pt: relembrar com carinho; conversar sobre o passado
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: At the reunion, the musicians reminisced about the concerts they had played together.
items.note: Usually refers to talking or thinking fondly about the past, often with other people.

items.pt: reminiscências; lembranças narradas do passado
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: Her memoir consists largely of reminiscences of life in a small coastal town.
items.note: Plural noun for remembered past experiences, especially in spoken or written accounts.

items.pt: óculos cor-de-rosa; visão idealizada do passado
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: He views his university days through rose-tinted spectacles and forgets the financial worries.
items.note: Figurative: seeing chiefly the pleasant aspects of the past; rose-coloured spectacles is also used.

items.pt: nostalgia; saudade de tempos passados
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: A wave of nostalgia washed over her when she found her childhood notebooks.
items.note: Warm, sometimes bittersweet feelings about a past time or place.

items.pt: uma sensação de nostalgia; saudade
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: The old photographs stirred a sense of nostalgia among the former students.
items.note: An established phrase to describe the feeling associated with memories.

items.pt: o que mais se destaca; o que mais chama a atenção
items.section: A · Looking back and sharing memories
items.example: What stands out from that period is how generously people shared their knowledge.
items.note: Beyond memories, stand out can highlight a particularly noticeable fact.

items.pt: arrepender-se de ter feito algo
items.example: I regret agreeing to the revised schedule before consulting the rest of the team.
items.note: Regret + -ing looks back at an action already taken; compare regret not doing something.

items.pt: arrepender-se de não ter feito algo
items.example: She regrets not learning another language when she had more free time.
items.note: Regret + not + -ing focuses on a missed action or opportunity.

items.pt: lamentar; sentir arrependimento
items.example: He expressed regret over the decision but stopped short of apologising.
items.note: As a noun or verb, regret indicates sadness about a choice or event; it need not imply wrongdoing.

items.pt: remorso; culpa profunda por um erro cometido
items.example: The former official expressed genuine remorse for misleading the public.
items.note: A strong feeling of guilt over an action considered wrong; stronger moral dimension than regret.

items.pt: não demonstrar remorso
items.example: Despite the harm she had caused, the manager showed no remorse.
items.note: A fixed collocation often used for somebody who seems unconcerned about wrongdoing.

items.pt: vergonha; sentimento de culpa ou humilhação
items.example: He felt deep shame about concealing the evidence from his colleagues.
items.note: Here shame refers to guilt or distress about behaviour; it is not merely social shyness.

items.pt: pontadas de culpa; culpa intensa e repentina
items.example: She felt pangs of guilt each time she passed the neglected community centre.
items.note: A pang is a sudden, sharp feeling, especially of guilt, regret or remorse.

items.pt: pontadas de remorso; crises repentinas de remorso
items.example: Occasional pangs of remorse made him question how he had treated his closest friend.
items.note: Pangs of remorse emphasises sudden painful feelings of moral guilt.

items.pt: uma pontada de consciência; súbita culpa
items.example: A pang of conscience prompted him to correct the inaccurate figures.
items.note: A sudden feeling that one has acted wrongly; the unit identifies conscience as a common partner of pang.

items.pt: arrepender-se amargamente do dia em que algo aconteceu
items.example: After the partnership collapsed, he rued the day he had signed the agreement.
items.note: Literary and emphatic expression for bitter regret; rue also combines with the fact that.

items.pt: lamentar profundamente o fato de que
items.example: She rues the fact that she never thanked her mentor properly.
items.note: Formal/literary wording, usually for a decision or omission with continuing consequences.
items.speechText: rue the fact that I left

items.pt: lamentar; expressar tristeza por uma perda
items.example: The author laments the disappearance of traditional local crafts.
items.note: A formal, somewhat literary verb for sadness about loss or undesirable change.

items.pt: lamentar o desaparecimento de; entristecer-se com o fim de
items.example: In her essay, she lamented the passing of the town’s independent bookshops.
items.note: A common literary pattern for mourning the end of an era, custom or institution.
items.speechText: lament the passing of an era

items.pt: lamentar uma perda; estar de luto por
items.example: Residents mourned the loss of the historic theatre after the fire.
items.note: Used for grief after a death and figuratively for the loss of valued things.

items.pt: lamentar oportunidades perdidas
items.example: Rather than mourn lost opportunities, she chose to apply for a new scholarship.
items.note: Literary collocation focusing on missed chances rather than a person’s death.

items.pt: consciência pesada
items.example: His guilty conscience eventually led him to admit what had happened.
items.note: Related to pangs of conscience; a longer-lasting sense of having done wrong.

units.title: Unit 78 — Agreement, disagreement and compromise
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 78. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Communication · agreement, dissent, negotiation and discretion
learningObjectives: Choose agreement verbs with their required prepositions and degrees of formality.
Distinguish dissent, discord, rift, split, division and controversy.
Discuss compromise, concessions and settlements with conventional collocations.
Express agreement emphatically and handle sensitive disagreements with discretion.

sectionsChecked: A · Agreement: sharing views and verb-preposition patterns

items.pt: corresponder a; estar de acordo com
items.example: The witness’s account tallied with the evidence from the security cameras.
items.note: Common for facts, figures or accounts that match; followed by with.

items.pt: concordar com uma opinião; corroborar
items.example: Several specialists concurred with the committee’s assessment of the risks.
items.note: Formal; used for shared judgements or opinions, with with.

items.pt: estar em total concordância com
items.example: The new recommendations are in full accord with the association’s principles.
items.note: Formal phrase expressing complete agreement or harmony, followed by with.
items.speechText: in full accord with the policy

items.pt: coincidir com; corresponder a
items.example: Our interpretation coincides with the findings of two independent research teams.
items.note: With opinions or evidence, indicates agreement; also used for events occurring at the same time.

items.pt: estar de acordo com normas; adequar-se a
items.example: The revised design must conform to the laboratory’s safety requirements.
items.note: Means meet an established rule, standard or expectation; normally takes to.

items.pt: aprovar; considerar algo correto ou adequado
items.example: Her supervisors approved of the decision to publish the unexpected findings.
items.note: Expresses a favourable opinion, distinct from official approval of an action; followed by of.

items.pt: aprovação; reconhecimento favorável
items.example: The plan received broad approval from researchers and local residents.
items.note: The noun corresponding to approve; approval can be formal authorisation or general support.

items.pt: receber aprovação; ser bem recebido
items.example: The proposed timetable met with the staff’s approval after several revisions.
items.note: A fixed pattern: a decision or action meets with somebody’s approval.

items.pt: concordar em discordar; encerrar a discussão mantendo opiniões diferentes
items.example: After an hour of debate, the two colleagues agreed to differ and moved on.
items.note: British English expression; each person retains their view without prolonging the dispute.

items.pt: chegar a um consenso
items.example: After several workshops, the research group reached a consensus on the methodology.
items.note: Reach a consensus highlights a broadly shared decision after discussion.

items.pt: consenso; concordância geral
items.example: There was little consensus about which proposal offered the best value.
items.note: A general agreement within a group; normally uncountable in this meaning.

items.pt: compartilhar uma opinião; ter o mesmo entendimento
items.example: The two authors share a view that public data should be independently audited.
items.note: More neutral than formal concur with; do not assume two people agree on all matters.

items.pt: concordância; anuência formal
items.example: The proposal was published with the concurrence of the independent reviewers.
items.note: A noun related to concur; more formal and less common than agreement.

items.pt: dissidência; oposição a uma opinião dominante
items.example: Dissent within the board grew as the financial implications became clearer.
items.note: Disagreement with an accepted policy, view or authority; often uncountable.

items.pt: desavença; falta de harmonia entre pessoas ou grupos
items.example: Years of discord among the shareholders prevented a coherent strategy.
items.note: Implies persistent lack of harmony, often accompanied by quarrels or tension.

items.pt: racha; ruptura na relação entre pessoas ou grupos
items.example: A public rift emerged between the party leadership and its younger members.
items.note: A serious division in a previously connected relationship or organisation.

items.pt: cisão; divisão efetiva de um grupo
items.example: The dispute over funding resulted in a split within the professional association.
items.note: A division that may lead to groups separating, not merely disagreeing.

items.pt: divergência; divisão entre pessoas ou facções
items.example: The proposed reforms caused deep division within the department.
items.note: More abstract and often more formal than a split; can be countable or uncountable.

items.pt: controvérsia; debate público acalorado
items.example: The decision to cancel the exhibition generated considerable controversy.
items.note: Public disagreement about an issue, often because it affects many people.

items.pt: causar polêmica; provocar controvérsia
items.example: The new admissions policy is likely to cause controversy across the sector.
items.note: A common collocation used when actions trigger substantial public disagreement.

items.pt: opiniões divergentes; posições dissidentes
items.example: The minutes recorded several dissenting views from members of the committee.
items.note: Dissenting describes opinions that differ from a dominant or official position.

items.pt: controverso; polêmico
items.example: The panel postponed its decision on the controversial development project.
items.note: Adjective from controversy; can refer to a decision, policy, figure or question.

items.pt: um racha cada vez maior
items.example: A growing rift between the two unions threatened the negotiations.
items.note: Describes escalating internal disagreement before a possible formal split.

items.pt: chegar a um acordo mediante concessões
items.example: The unions and management reached a compromise over the revised shift pattern.
items.note: Each party usually makes concessions rather than getting everything it wants.

items.pt: chegar a um acordo sobre uma questão específica
items.example: The residents reached a compromise over access to the shared gardens.
items.note: The source combines reach a compromise with over to identify the disputed issue.

items.pt: ceder em; aceitar concessões sobre algo
items.example: Neither side was willing to compromise on the core safety requirements.
items.note: Compromise on an issue identifies where concessions may or may not be made.

items.pt: fazer concessões a; ceder parcialmente às reivindicações de
items.example: The university made concessions to students over library opening hours.
items.note: Formal negotiation phrase; concessions are demands or positions partly yielded.

items.pt: uma concessão; cedência parcial em uma negociação
items.example: Extending the deadline was the government’s main concession during the talks.
items.note: A concession is something given up or granted to facilitate agreement.

items.pt: admitir um ponto; ceder em uma argumentação
items.example: The chair conceded that the opposition had raised a legitimate concern.
items.note: Often acknowledges a point reluctantly; corresponds to the noun concession in exercise 78.3.

items.pt: chegar a um acordo que encerra uma disputa
items.example: The company and the former employees reached a settlement after mediation.
items.note: A settlement resolves a dispute, particularly in industrial, legal or commercial contexts.

items.pt: um acordo; resolução formal de um conflito
items.example: Both parties described the settlement as fair and sustainable.
items.note: Noun for the outcome of a dispute-resolution process; not merely a verbal compromise.

items.pt: agir com discrição e bom senso; usar discernimento
items.example: Managers should exercise discretion when discussing confidential medical information.
items.note: Formal collocation for using judgement sensitively in potentially delicate situations.

items.pt: discrição; discernimento ao decidir ou falar
items.example: The investigator handled the witness’s identity with considerable discretion.
items.note: The ability to judge what is appropriate, especially when sensitive information is involved.

items.pt: discreto; reservado e cuidadoso
items.example: Please be discreet about the changes until the team has been informed.
items.note: The adjective linked to discretion; not the same as discrete meaning separate or distinct.

items.pt: Com certeza!; totalmente de acordo!
items.example: We ought to explain the risks before proceeding. Absolutely!
items.note: A strong conversational agreement; stress and intonation can signal enthusiasm.

items.pt: Exatamente!; é isso mesmo!
items.example: The issue is not cost alone but long-term reliability. Precisely!
items.note: Signals strong agreement, especially with an accurately formulated point.
